note: The sixteen children of Valentino Defranceschi and Helena/Elena, read out of the Liber Baptizatorum and the burial register of Fiume on 6 September 2026, re-checked against the FamilySearch index on 20 September and then **read back on the film, page by page, the same day**. **Every child cites the image it stands on.** The list stood at fourteen until the index turned up a fifteenth, **Jacobus Vincentius, baptised 21 July 1757** — the tenth son, and the one that makes the family's own count come out. **It stood at fifteen until 20 September, when a sixteenth was found the hard way**: not in any index, but on **image 146 of the film**, during a frame-by-frame sweep of the 1746–1750 gap — **Francisca Matthæa, baptised 13 October 1747**. She is a daughter, so the ten sons are untouched.
heading: Valentino's sixteen children, out of the Fiume register
lead: Kobler's earliest Fiume household is «Valentino Defranceschi, venuto dalla Carnia, fu fatto Cittadino nel 1739». The register says what that citizenship was for: **he had been baptising children there since 1737**, and he went on doing it for twenty years. **Ten sons and six daughters.** The family account has always said *ten sons*, and for as long as this archive had fourteen children it could only count nine; **with Jacobus Vincentius the sons come out at ten exactly** — and the sixteenth child, found on the film on 20 September, is a **daughter**, so that count still holds. Five of the sixteen are known only from the burial register. And the register does one more thing the index cannot: **by 1747 it already calls the father D.nus Valentinus and stands Ill.mus over the font** — a Carnian immigrant's children sponsored by Fiume patricians, and in 1754 by a **free baroness**.
source: Liber Baptizatorum and the burial register of the collegiate church of St Vitus, Fiume — read 6 September 2026, and every entry re-found on the film on 20 September 2026. Baptisms are **film 005497925**, burials **film 005497941**. **All sixteen children cite the image they stand on**; eleven carry a FamilySearch index entry, and the five that appear in no index — *Ignatius Francus Mattheus 1745, **Francisca Matthæa 1747**, Vitus Joannes Baptista 1751, Aloysius Rochus 1754, Rosalia Francisca 1755* — were found on the pages themselves. Four of them were recovered by interpolating between dated frames, **all four exactly where the 6 September reading said they were**. **Francisca Matthæa was different: nothing pointed at her.** She turned up because the 1746–1750 gap was being swept frame by frame for a *son*, and image 146 held a daughter instead. *(doc — every row cites an image.)*
